answers.ask: No setting was given - should the maps be modern military, sci-fi, or bright and cartoonish?
answers.answer: Use a bright, cartoonish shooter style so the weapons, skins, and wraps feel fun and readable.

answers.ask: Which space should be built first: the lobby, the practice range, or a match map?
answers.answer: Build the lobby first, since it is the hub for matchmaking, weapon unlocks, skin boxes, wrap boxes, and entering the practice arena.

answers.ask: Which game modes do you want - team deathmatch, free-for-all, objective modes?
answers.answer: Include team deathmatch and free-for-all first; keep objective modes out of the initial build.

config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this Shooter map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Lane Network: Parallel routes, classically three, channelling team traffic into predictable engagement fronts.

INCLUDE:
- Tactical Cover Arrays: Waist-high (3–4 studs) and full-body (7–8 studs) cover distributed evenly across every lane.
- Opposing Team Bases: Balanced bases at opposite ends of the map, each enclosed so it is not overlooked from open ground.
- Lane Pinch Point: Narrow transitions where lanes meet, concentrating fights into contested ground.
- Practice Targets: Static and popping targets set at graded distances downrange — plates, silhouettes, bullseyes — arranged so the player can read which distance they are hitting.
- Weapon Bench: A bench or rack behind the firing line where players pick and swap the weapon they are practising with.
